newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore HSFO soft on crude falls over Iraq news.
newsitem.headline: Singapore HSFO soft on crude falls over Iraq news.

text.p: High sulphur fuel oil prices on Tuesday were assessed softer on a weaker crude market but buying interest from a local trader may limit the slide, traders said.
High sulphur, 180 centistoke fuel oil was quoted at $124.5/$125.5 per tonne on Monday.
Traders said the falls in the crude market in both London and New York after news Iraq had agreed to all conditions in the oil-for-food deal, will prompt a slip in fuel oil prices.
Traders said Chinese demand remained depressed as offers remained too high, traders said.
But a bid seen late Tuesday by a local trader at a low of $120 per tonne for mid December loading cargoes, compared to trades done on Monday at up to a high of $125 per tonne.
If the bid is firm, there would be an offer to take that bid out, a trader said.
In the swaps market, fuel oil was quoted unchanged from earlier Tuesday in quiet trade with December was last quoted at $120.00/$121.00.
